target.statement: Random Forest with plain strategy (default 0.5 threshold) on credit-card fraud dataset attains F1 = 0.861 ± 0.021 under 5-fold nested CV
target.table_ref: Table 1, row 'Random Forest / plain', column F1
target.dataset: Kaggle credit-card fraud (Dal Pozzolo et al., 284,807 rows, 492 positives)

compute.basis: Paper states Study A runs in ~9 minutes on a consumer laptop with only scikit-learn/imbalanced-learn; 5-fold RF (100 trees, depth 16) on 285k rows is CPU-trivial, plus Kaggle download and install time.

blockers: Code links are relative paths in the PDF with no repository URL; the actual code/data release location is not given, so the harness may need to be re-implemented from the protocol description
Kaggle dataset requires a free Kaggle account/API token to download
Exact fold seeds and preprocessing details must be matched to hit 0.861 ± 0.021 precisely
title: When Single-Dataset Conclusions Fail: A 45-Task Study of Threshold Tuning and Resampling for Imbalanced Classification
